Vacillate

/VASS-uh-layt/ - the stress falls on VASS · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Vacillate means to fluctuate or hesitate between choices.

All autumn the farm vacillated between selling the herd and expanding it, buying feed one week and printing sale flyers the next.

Worked Example

Bree vacillated between the two wedding venues for months — booking the orchard in spring, switching to the ballroom when the forecast turned, then switching back — until both quietly gave her dates away.

Vacillate is more specific than 'waver': a waver is one wobble of resolve, while vacillating is a repeated swing between choices — committing first to one side, then the other, and landing on neither.

How Strong Is It? — hedge → waver → vacillate

hedge vs. vacillate

hedge vs. vacillate: To hedge is the mildest move — you avoid committing in words while standing still; it stops far short of vacillating.

waver vs. vacillate

waver vs. vacillate: To waver stops short of vacillating: wavering is one wobble of resolve, while vacillating swings you fully from side to side and back.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — vacill

Root — vacill: to sway, to totter (Latin vacillare)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: verb ending

Put it together

Put it together: Vacill- (to sway, from Latin vacillare) + -ate (verb ending) = to sway in place. The word's original tottering is still visible: a vacillating mind leans one way, then the other, never planting its feet.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: Vacillate comes from Latin vacillare, 'to sway or totter.' The -ate is a common verb ending, but the vacill- root appears in no other English word, so there is no cousin to point to.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal

Vacillate is the formal word for swinging between positions — voters, boards, and buyers vacillate. Its unit-mate dither fusses without ever choosing; vacillating chooses constantly, a different side each time. For numbers that rise and fall, the word is fluctuate, not vacillate.
